    *   Action: Player switches to Door $Z$.

*   $P(\text{Sticky}) = 1/3$
*   $P(\text{Shifting}) = 1/3$

    *   $P(\text{Win} | \text{Random}) = 2/3$ (Standard probability)

*   **Posterior Probabilities:**
    *   $P(\text{Sticky} | E) \propto (1/3) \times 0 = 0$. The probability of the Sticky rule is now **0**.
    *   $P(\text{Shifting} | E) \propto (1/3) \times 1 = 1/3$.
    *   $P(\text{Random} | E) \propto (1/3) \times (2/3) = 2/9$.

    Normalizing the remaining probabilities (Shifting and Random):

    *   $P(\text{Random} | E) = (2/9) / (5/9) = 2/5 = 0.4$.

There is a 60% chance the rule is "Shifting" and a 40% chance the rule is "Random". The "Sticky" rule has been ruled out.

        $$P(\text{Win} | \text{Switch}) = 0.6 \times 1 + 0.4 \times \frac{2}{3}$$

### Step-by-Step Reasoning

Using Bayes' Theorem to find the posterior probability of each rule given the evidence ($E$):
$$P(Rule | E) = \frac{P(E | Rule) \times P(Rule)}{P(E)}$$
